careers.name: Welder
careers.does: Joins metal parts together with intense heat to build bridges, ships, trucks and machines.
careers.path: High school, then a welding certificate (a few months to a year) or an apprenticeship.
careers.try: Build something with a hot glue gun, or watch a welding demo at a career fair.

careers.name: CNC Machinist
careers.does: Programs and runs computer-controlled machines that cut metal into exact parts, down to a hair's width.
careers.path: High school, then a technical program or apprenticeship.
careers.try: Try a CAD program like Tinkercad and design a part.
careers.oohTitle: Machinists and Tool and Die Makers
careers.eduNote: Machinists typically need a high school diploma or equivalent

careers.name: Industrial Engineer
careers.does: Figures out how a factory, hospital or warehouse can work faster, safer and with less waste.
careers.path: A bachelor's degree in engineering.
careers.try: Time how long it takes to make a sandwich, then redesign the steps to make it faster.

careers.name: Robotics Technician
careers.does: Builds, tests and repairs the robots that weld, pack and move things in factories.
careers.path: A two-year degree in robotics or engineering technology.
careers.try: Join a robotics club or build a kit robot.
careers.oohTitle: Electro-mechanical and Mechatronics Technologists and Technicians

careers.name: Veterinarian
careers.does: Diagnoses and treats sick and injured animals, from pets to farm animals.
careers.path: A bachelor's degree, then four years of veterinary school.
careers.try: Volunteer at an animal shelter or join 4-H.

careers.name: Veterinary Technician
careers.does: Helps vets by taking X-rays, running lab tests and caring for animals during surgery.
careers.path: A two-year veterinary technology degree and a license.
careers.try: Help care for a pet and keep a log of its health.

careers.name: Food Scientist
careers.does: Invents new foods and makes sure food is safe, tasty and lasts longer.
careers.path: A bachelor's degree in food science, chemistry or biology.
careers.try: Bake a recipe three ways, change one thing each time, and compare.

careers.name: Farmer or Rancher
careers.does: Runs a farm or ranch: plants crops, raises animals, fixes equipment and sells what they grow.
careers.path: Many learn by working on a farm; an agriculture degree helps.
careers.try: Grow vegetables in a pot or school garden.
careers.oohTitle: Farmers, Ranchers, and Other Agricultural Managers

careers.name: Graphic Designer
careers.does: Designs logos, posters, apps and packaging that catch your eye and make ideas clear.
careers.path: A bachelor's degree or a strong portfolio of work.
careers.try: Design a poster for a school event.

careers.name: Animator
careers.does: Creates the moving characters and effects in movies, shows and video games.
careers.path: A bachelor's degree in animation or art, plus a demo reel.
careers.try: Make a flip book or a stop-motion video with a phone.

careers.name: Musician
careers.does: Plays, sings, writes and records music for concerts, recordings, places of worship, schools and games.
careers.path: Years of practice; some study music in college.
careers.try: Join band, choir or orchestra, or write your own song.

careers.name: Photographer
careers.does: Takes photos for news, weddings, sports, products and art.
careers.path: Training on the job or in college, and a portfolio.
careers.try: Do a photo challenge: one great photo a day for a week.

careers.name: Fashion Designer
careers.does: Sketches and creates clothing, shoes and accessories.
careers.path: A bachelor's degree in fashion design, or a portfolio.
careers.try: Redesign an old T-shirt or sketch a clothing line.

careers.name: Video Game Designer
careers.does: Plans the levels, rules and stories of video games so they are fun to play.
careers.path: A bachelor's degree in game design or computer science, plus games you have made.
careers.try: Make a game in Scratch or design a board game.

careers.name: Film and Video Editor
careers.does: Cuts and arranges video clips, sound and effects to tell a story.
careers.path: A bachelor's degree or experience and a reel.
careers.try: Film and edit a one-minute video about your school.
careers.oohTitle: Film and Video Editors and Camera Operators

careers.name: Interior Designer
careers.does: Plans rooms that look great and work well: colors, furniture, lighting and layout.
careers.path: A bachelor's degree; many states require a license.
careers.try: Draw a floor plan of your dream bedroom.

careers.name: Writer or Author
careers.does: Writes books, articles, scripts, games and websites.
careers.path: Usually a bachelor's degree, and lots of writing.
careers.try: Write for the school paper or start a story journal.

careers.name: Actor
careers.does: Brings characters to life on stage, in films, shows and commercials.
careers.path: Acting classes, practice and many auditions.
careers.try: Try out for a school play.

careers.name: Producer or Director
careers.does: Leads the team that makes a movie, show, play or podcast, from idea to finished product.
careers.path: A bachelor's degree and years of work in media.
careers.try: Direct a short video with friends.

careers.name: Electrician
careers.does: Installs and repairs the wiring that brings power and light to homes and buildings.
careers.path: A four-to-five-year paid apprenticeship and a license.
careers.try: Build a simple circuit with a battery, wire and bulb.

careers.name: Carpenter
careers.does: Builds and repairs the wooden frames, stairs, cabinets and floors of buildings.
careers.path: An apprenticeship or on-the-job training.
careers.try: Build a birdhouse or a shelf.

careers.name: Plumber
careers.does: Installs and fixes the pipes that bring clean water in and take wastewater out.
careers.path: A four-to-five-year paid apprenticeship and a license.
careers.try: Help fix a leaky faucet at home (with an adult).

careers.name: Architect
careers.does: Designs buildings that are safe, useful and beautiful.
careers.path: A degree in architecture, internship years and a license.
careers.try: Design a house in Minecraft or on graph paper.

careers.name: Civil Engineer
careers.does: Designs roads, bridges, tunnels and water systems.
careers.path: A bachelor's degree in civil engineering.
careers.try: Build a bridge from craft sticks and test how much it holds.

careers.name: HVAC Technician
careers.does: Installs and repairs heating, air conditioning and refrigeration systems.
careers.path: A certificate program (six months to two years) or apprenticeship.
careers.try: Find out how your home is heated and cooled.
careers.oohTitle: Heating, Air Conditioning, and Refrigeration Mechanics and Installers

careers.name: Heavy Equipment Operator
careers.does: Drives bulldozers, cranes and excavators to move earth and build roads.
careers.path: On-the-job training or an apprenticeship.
careers.try: Visit a construction site viewing area or a heavy equipment show.

careers.name: Software Developer
careers.does: Designs and writes the code for apps, websites, games and the software inside cars and phones.
careers.path: A bachelor's degree in computer science, or strong skills and projects.
careers.try: Learn to code with Scratch or Python.
careers.oohTitle: Software Developers, Quality Assurance Analysts, and Testers

careers.name: Cybersecurity Analyst
careers.does: Protects computer networks from hackers and investigates attacks.
careers.path: A bachelor's degree in computing, plus certifications.
careers.try: Try a student cybersecurity game like picoCTF.

careers.name: Data Scientist
careers.does: Finds patterns in huge amounts of data to answer questions and make predictions.
careers.path: A bachelor's or master's degree in data science, statistics or math.
careers.try: Survey your class and make a chart of the results.

careers.name: Web Developer
careers.does: Builds websites and makes them fast, good-looking and easy to use.
careers.path: A degree, a coding bootcamp or self-taught skills and a portfolio.
careers.try: Build a web page about your favorite hobby.

careers.name: IT Support Specialist
careers.does: Helps people fix computer problems and keeps a school or company's tech running.
careers.path: Some college or certifications.
careers.try: Help family members set up a new device.
careers.eduNote: user support specialists typically need to complete some college courses

careers.name: Elementary Teacher
careers.does: Teaches young students reading, math, science and how to be part of a class.
careers.path: A bachelor's degree and a teaching license.
careers.try: Read to younger kids or help at a summer camp.

careers.name: Preschool Teacher
careers.does: Helps 3- and 4-year-olds learn through play, songs and stories.
careers.path: A certificate or two-year degree; some states require a bachelor's.
careers.try: Babysit or help in a children's program.

careers.name: School Counselor
careers.does: Helps students with school, friendships and planning their future.
careers.path: A master's degree in counseling.
careers.try: Be a peer mentor or buddy for a new student.
careers.oohTitle: School and Career Counselors and Advisors

careers.name: Librarian
careers.does: Helps people find information, runs programs and chooses books and media.
careers.path: A master's degree in library science.
careers.try: Volunteer at your school or public library.

careers.name: Coach
careers.does: Trains athletes and teams, plans practices and makes game-day decisions.
careers.path: Experience in the sport; many have a bachelor's degree.
careers.try: Help coach a younger kids' team.

careers.name: Wind Turbine Technician
careers.does: Climbs giant wind turbines to inspect and repair them.
careers.path: A certificate or two-year degree.
careers.try: Build a small wind turbine from a kit or cardboard.

careers.name: Solar Panel Installer
careers.does: Installs solar panels on roofs and in solar farms.
careers.path: On-the-job training or a short certificate.
careers.try: Track how much sun your house gets in a day.

careers.name: Environmental Scientist
careers.does: Studies air, water and soil to protect people and nature from pollution.
careers.path: A bachelor's degree in a natural science.
careers.try: Test the water in a local creek with a science kit.

careers.name: Wildlife Biologist
careers.does: Studies animals in the wild and how to protect them and their homes.
careers.path: A bachelor's degree; many have a master's.
careers.try: Keep a nature journal of birds or animals you see.

careers.name: Power Line Worker
careers.does: Builds and repairs the power lines that carry electricity, often after storms.
careers.path: A certificate and a long paid apprenticeship.
careers.try: Learn how electricity gets from a power plant to your outlet.

careers.name: Meteorologist
careers.does: Studies the atmosphere to forecast weather and track storms.
careers.path: A bachelor's degree in meteorology or atmospheric science.
careers.try: Keep a weather log and make your own forecast.

careers.name: Accountant
careers.does: Tracks money for people and businesses, prepares taxes and checks that records are correct.
careers.path: A bachelor's degree in accounting.
careers.try: Keep a budget for your allowance or a club.

careers.name: Financial Advisor
careers.does: Helps people plan how to save, invest and reach goals like college or retirement.
careers.path: A bachelor's degree and licenses.
careers.try: Try a stock market simulation game.

careers.name: Actuary
careers.does: Uses math and statistics to measure risk for insurance companies.
careers.path: A bachelor's degree and a series of exams.
careers.try: Run a probability experiment with dice and chart the results.

careers.name: Registered Nurse
careers.does: Cares for patients, gives medicine, watches for changes and teaches families.
careers.path: A two-year or four-year nursing degree and a license.
careers.try: Take a first-aid or babysitting safety class.

careers.name: Family Doctor
careers.does: Diagnoses and treats illness and helps people of all ages stay healthy.
careers.path: A bachelor's degree, four years of medical school and three or more years of residency.
careers.try: Join a science club or health careers program.

careers.name: Physician Assistant
careers.does: Examines patients, diagnoses illnesses and prescribes treatment as part of a doctor-led team.
careers.path: A bachelor's degree, then a two-year master's program.
careers.try: Learn how the body works with a model or app.

careers.name: Physical Therapist
careers.does: Helps people recover from injuries and move better through exercise.
careers.path: A doctor of physical therapy degree (about three years after college).
careers.try: Learn the muscles you use in your favorite sport.

careers.name: Dental Hygienist
careers.does: Cleans teeth, takes X-rays and teaches people how to keep their mouths healthy.
careers.path: A two-year degree and a license.
careers.try: Find out why fluoride protects teeth.

careers.name: Paramedic
careers.does: Rushes to emergencies and gives life-saving care on the way to the hospital.
careers.path: EMT training, then a paramedic certificate or degree.
careers.try: Learn CPR and first aid.

careers.name: Pharmacist
careers.does: Prepares medicines and makes sure people take them safely.
careers.path: A doctor of pharmacy degree (about six years after high school).
careers.try: Find out how medicines are tested before they are sold.

careers.name: Social Worker
careers.does: Helps children and families get through hard times and find support.
careers.path: A bachelor's or master's degree in social work.
careers.try: Volunteer with a food bank or community group.
careers.eduNote: A bachelor's degree in social work (BSW) is the most common requirement for entry-level nonclinical social worker positions.

careers.name: Psychologist
careers.does: Helps people understand their thoughts and feelings and studies how the mind works.
careers.path: A master's or doctoral degree in psychology (clinical psychologists need a doctorate).
careers.try: Read about how memory works and test it on yourself.
careers.eduNote: Psychologists typically need at least a master's degree to enter the occupation.

careers.name: Medical Assistant
careers.does: Checks patients in, takes vital signs and helps doctors with exams.
careers.path: A certificate program (about a year).
careers.try: Learn to take a pulse and blood pressure.

careers.name: Athletic Trainer
careers.does: Prevents and treats sports injuries for athletes.
careers.path: A master's degree in athletic training and a license.
careers.try: Ask your school's athletic trainer about their job.

careers.name: Chef
careers.does: Creates menus, cooks and runs a restaurant kitchen.
careers.path: Experience in kitchens; some go to culinary school.
careers.try: Cook dinner for your family once a week.

careers.name: Restaurant Cook
careers.does: Prepares meals quickly and carefully during busy restaurant shifts.
careers.path: On-the-job training.
careers.try: Learn five recipes you can cook on your own.
careers.eduNote: Most cooks learn their skills through on-the-job training and work-related experience.

careers.name: Event Planner
careers.does: Plans weddings, concerts, conferences and festivals so everything goes right.
careers.path: A bachelor's degree or experience.
careers.try: Plan a class party or school event.

careers.name: Hotel Manager
careers.does: Runs a hotel: guests, staff, budgets and solving problems.
careers.path: Experience in hotels; many have a hospitality degree.
careers.try: Plan a pretend weekend trip and compare three places to stay online.

careers.name: Flight Attendant
careers.does: Keeps passengers safe and comfortable on flights.
careers.path: High school and airline training.
careers.try: Learn some phrases in another language.

careers.name: Hairstylist
careers.does: Cuts, colors and styles hair and helps clients look their best.
careers.path: Cosmetology school (about a year) and a license.
careers.try: Practice braids or styles with family or friends.

careers.name: Business Manager
careers.does: Runs the day-to-day work of a company: people, budgets and goals.
careers.path: A bachelor's degree and work experience.
careers.try: Run a small business like a lemonade or craft stand.

careers.name: Human Resources Specialist
careers.does: Hires new workers, helps employees and makes workplaces fair.
careers.path: A bachelor's degree.
careers.try: Interview an adult about how they got hired.

careers.name: Project Manager
careers.does: Plans big projects, sets deadlines and keeps a team on track.
careers.path: A bachelor's degree and experience; certifications help.
careers.try: Plan a group project with a timeline and roles.

careers.name: Marketing Manager
careers.does: Plans how to get people excited about a product, brand or cause.
careers.path: A bachelor's degree and experience in marketing.
careers.try: Create an ad campaign for a school event.

careers.name: Real Estate Agent
careers.does: Helps people buy and sell homes.
careers.path: A pre-licensing course and a state license.
careers.try: Compare three homes for sale online and pick the best value.
careers.oohTitle: Real Estate Brokers and Sales Agents

careers.name: Public Relations Specialist
careers.does: Shapes how the public sees a company, team or person: press releases, events and social media.
careers.path: A bachelor's degree in communications or journalism.
careers.try: Write a news release about something great at your school.

careers.name: Market Research Analyst
careers.does: Studies what people want to buy and why, using surveys and data.
careers.path: A bachelor's degree.
careers.try: Survey classmates about a snack and present the results.

careers.name: Firefighter
careers.does: Puts out fires, rescues people and answers medical emergencies.
careers.path: Fire academy training and EMT certification.
careers.try: Learn fire safety and visit a fire station open house.

careers.name: Police Officer
careers.does: Protects people, responds to emergencies and enforces laws.
careers.path: Police academy training; some departments require college.
careers.try: Join a youth explorer program.
careers.eduNote: Police and detective applicants must have at least a high school diploma or equivalent

careers.name: Lawyer
careers.does: Advises people and argues cases in court.
careers.path: A bachelor's degree, three years of law school and a bar exam.
careers.try: Join debate or mock trial.

careers.name: Paralegal
careers.does: Helps lawyers research laws, organize evidence and prepare documents.
careers.path: A two-year degree or certificate.
careers.try: Research how a law in your state was made.

careers.name: Urban Planner
careers.does: Plans how towns grow: parks, housing, transit and roads.
careers.path: A master's degree in planning.
careers.try: Design a better park or street for your neighborhood.

careers.name: 911 Dispatcher
careers.does: Answers emergency calls and sends police, fire and ambulances.
careers.path: On-the-job training and certification.
careers.try: Learn what to say when you call 911.

careers.name: Forensic Science Technician
careers.does: Collects and tests evidence from crime scenes.
careers.path: A bachelor's degree in a natural science.
careers.try: Try fingerprinting or chromatography with a science kit.

careers.name: Airline Pilot
careers.does: Flies passengers and cargo safely around the world.
careers.path: A bachelor's degree, flight training, FAA licenses and about 1,500 hours of flying.
careers.try: Try a flight simulator or visit an airport.
careers.eduNote: Airline pilots typically need a bachelor's degree and experience as a commercial or military pilot.

careers.name: Truck Driver
careers.does: Drives big trucks to deliver goods across the country.
careers.path: A commercial driver's license (a few weeks of training).
careers.try: Plan a road trip route on a map.

careers.name: Logistician
careers.does: Plans how products get from factories to stores and doorsteps on time.
careers.path: A bachelor's degree.
careers.try: Track a package and map the route it took.

careers.name: Auto Technician
careers.does: Diagnoses and repairs cars, including electric vehicles.
careers.path: A certificate or two-year program.
careers.try: Learn to check a car's oil and tire pressure.

careers.name: Aircraft Mechanic
careers.does: Inspects and repairs airplanes so they are safe to fly.
careers.path: An 18-to-24-month FAA-approved school and a license.
careers.try: Build a model airplane and learn what each part does.
careers.oohTitle: Aircraft and Avionics Equipment Mechanics and Technicians

careers.name: Air Traffic Controller
careers.does: Guides airplanes safely through the sky and on runways.
careers.path: An associate's or bachelor's degree from an FAA-approved program (or work experience), then FAA Academy training; most must apply before age 31.
careers.try: Watch a live flight-tracking map.

careers.name: Aerospace Engineer
careers.does: Designs airplanes, rockets and satellites.
careers.path: A bachelor's degree in aerospace engineering.
careers.try: Build and launch a bottle rocket.

careers.name: Administrative Assistant
careers.does: Keeps an office running: schedules, files, phone calls and helping visitors.
careers.path: High school, then training on the job; some take office or computer courses.
careers.try: Organize a family calendar for one month.

careers.name: Retail Sales Worker
careers.does: Helps customers find what they need, answers questions and rings up sales in a store.
careers.path: Training on the job; no diploma is needed to start.
careers.try: Describe your favorite product in three sentences that would make a friend want it.

careers.name: Computer Research Scientist
careers.does: Invents new ways to use computers, like smarter AI and faster, safer software.
careers.path: A master's degree in computer science; some go on to a doctorate.
careers.try: Try a free coding or AI lesson online.

careers.name: Childcare Worker
careers.does: Cares for young children, plans play and learning, and keeps them safe.
careers.path: High school; many states also ask for childcare training or a certificate.
careers.try: Help a younger cousin or neighbor learn a game, with a grown-up nearby.

careers.name: Teacher Assistant
careers.does: Works beside a teacher, helping students one on one or in small groups.
careers.path: Some college, or passing a test of reading, writing and math skills.
careers.try: Help a younger student practice reading.

careers.name: Home Health Aide
careers.does: Helps older adults and people with disabilities with daily care in their homes.
careers.path: High school; many agencies require a short training course and a test.
careers.try: Help an older neighbor or relative with a chore.
careers.oohTitle: Home Health and Personal Care Aides

careers.name: Bookkeeper
careers.does: Keeps track of the money a business earns and spends.
careers.path: Some college courses in accounting; many learn the rest on the job.
careers.try: Track your own spending or savings for a month in a table.

careers.name: Warehouse Worker
careers.does: Moves, packs and loads goods in a warehouse so orders ship on time.
careers.path: Training on the job; some also earn a forklift certificate.
careers.try: Pack a box so nothing inside can move, then label it.

careers.name: Drafter
careers.does: Turns architects' and engineers' ideas into detailed drawings on a computer.
careers.path: A two-year degree in drafting or computer-aided design (CAD).
careers.try: Draw a floor plan of your room to scale on graph paper.

careers.name: Environmental Technician
careers.does: Tests air, water and soil for pollution and helps keep them clean.
careers.path: A two-year degree in science or an environmental program.
careers.try: Test water from two places with a pool or aquarium test kit and compare.
